decisions.reason: Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT states the full last-value flag method, including 'Y' at Visit 12, while its attached CL.AVISIT enumerates visit labels and excludes Y. Original MT.ADLBC.AVISIT (line 4836) and workbook Methods!D74 confirm that this is attached to AVISIT, so the documented conflict is real.

Define-XML ADLBC.PARAM and workbook Methods!D80 concatenate LB.LBTEST, '(', LB.LBSTRESU and ')' without a space, which the literal PARAM probe follows. The full CL.PARAM_ADLBC codelist supplies the space used by PARAM__CODELIST_SPACING, and the reported differences are exactly that space.

The blank quote omits the actual rule: Define-XML ADLBC.BASE and original MT.ADLBC.BASE (line 4842), also workbook Methods!D75, state LB.LBSTNRHI without a baseline condition. No ADLBC value-level metadata overrides that source, and the reported source-versus-reference differences therefore support CR-3.

Define-XML ADLBC.CHG states Significant digits: 5 and AVAL - BASE, also workbook Variables!G127 and Methods!D79, but supplies no half-away rounding instruction. The literal CHG probe adds that algorithm; CHG__UNROUNDED confirms the missing-versus-zero discrepancy, but does not make the rounded literal column faithful under CR-5.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO states Significant digits: 1 and AVAL / A1LO, also workbook Variables!G130 and Methods!D83, without a half-away rounding instruction. The literal probe adds that algorithm, while the unrounded division reproduces the reference, so the reported precision difference does not establish CR-5's as-written premise.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI states Significant digits: 1 and AVAL / A1HI, also workbook Variables!G131 and Methods!D82, without a half-away rounding instruction. The literal probe adds that algorithm, while the unrounded division reproduces the reference, so the reported precision difference does not establish CR-5's as-written premise.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO states AVAL / A1LO at baseline and Significant digits: 1, also workbook Methods!D78 and Variables!G132, without a half-away rounding instruction. The literal probe adds that algorithm to the baseline ratio; its unrounded whole-ratio reading reproduces the reference, so the literal-rule premise of CR-5 is unsupported.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI states AVAL / A1HI at baseline and Significant digits: 1, also workbook Methods!D77 and Variables!G133, without a half-away rounding instruction. The literal probe adds that algorithm to the baseline ratio; its unrounded whole-ratio reading reproduces the reference, so the literal-rule premise of CR-5 is unsupported.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANL01FL and workbook Methods!D72 specify equality to max(ALBTRVAL), but do not specify the maximum's grouping or eligible records. The literal probe assumes a dataset-wide maximum, while ADRG page-8's record structure selects neither that scope nor the subject/parameter alternative, so the mismatches do not establish a uniquely as-written CR-5 test.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states the signed maximum and Significant digits: 3, also workbook Methods!D71 and Variables!G135, but supplies no half-away rounding instruction. The literal probe adds that algorithm; ALBTRVAL__UNROUNDED independently confirms the signed-arithmetic discrepancy, but does not make the rounded literal column faithful under CR-5.

The full Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND method assigns Y for the low condition, while the same section's CL.LNH permits only L, N and H. Original MT.ADLBC.ANRIND (line 4830) and workbook Methods!D73 retain Y, so the conflict is not an extraction typo.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL and workbook Methods!D70 require early discontinuation and the last assessment during treatment, but do not define a closed TRTSDT-to-TRTEDT interval, date-tie handling or derived-row propagation. ADSL.DISCONFL and ADSL.VISNUMEN support candidate sources through their labels, but the literal probe adds those scope choices, so its mismatch tests an interpretation rather than a uniquely as-written CR-5 rule.

Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT's full method, confirmed by original MT.ADLBC.AVISIT (line 4836), explicitly assigns Y at Visit 12. The eot row rule instead assigns End of Treatment to AVISIT, so the executable clause differs even though the documented method appears misplaced.

Define-XML ADLBC.ADY and original MT.ADLBC.ADY (line 4807) state LB.LBDY. The executable ADY computes study_day from ADT and TRTSDT and never reads LB.LBDY; original SDTM COMPMETHOD.STUDY_DAY instead references RFSTDTC, so the named source has no executable counterpart under CR-4.

Define-XML ADLBC.BASE and original MT.ADLBC.BASE (line 4842), confirmed by workbook Methods!D75, state LB.LBSTNRHI. Executable BASE instead selects AVAL on ABLFL='Y', tracing to LB.LBSTRESN, so its source and computation differ from the actual documented rule under CR-4.

Define-XML ADLBC.CHG and workbook Methods!D79 state AVAL - BASE without a visit exception. Executable CHG adds a VISITNUM=1 missing branch, for which the retained sections and workbook provide no counterpart.

Define-XML ADLBC.A1LO and original MT.ADLBC.A1LO (line 4797) name LB.LBSTNRLO. Executable A1LO reads _r_LO=LB.LBSTNRLO, including EOTFB.LBSTNRLO on eot2, so CR-4's permitted intermediate path reaches the documented source.

Define-XML ADLBC.A1HI and original MT.ADLBC.A1HI (line 4792) name LB.LBSTNRHI. Executable A1HI reads _r_HI=LB.LBSTNRHI, including EOTFB.LBSTNRHI on eot2, so CR-4's permitted intermediate path reaches the documented source.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO and workbook Methods!D78 place the ratio AVAL / A1LO at baseline. Executable BASE / A1LO baseline-selects only the numerator and retains the current record's denominator, so it does not express the whole-ratio baseline condition even though both readings agree on these data.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI and workbook Methods!D77 place the ratio AVAL / A1HI at baseline. Executable BASE / A1HI baseline-selects only the numerator and retains the current record's denominator, so it does not express the whole-ratio baseline condition even though both readings agree on these data.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANL01FL and workbook Methods!D72 flag equality to max(ALBTRVAL). The _RN_ANL/_WINLB chain selects a sequence-number winner and ANL01FL tests LBSEQ, which does not express the documented equality rule for all tied maxima.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL's full signed maximum, also workbook Methods!D71, uses LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN). Executable _UPPER_DISTANCE adds ABS around that difference; AVAL currently copies LBSTRESN, but that equivalence does not remove the sign change.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL's full signed maximum, also workbook Methods!D71, uses (.5*LLN)-LBSTRESN. Executable _LOWER_DISTANCE adds ABS around that difference, which changes the documented signed computation.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND and workbook Methods!D73 explicitly assign Y for AVAL below half the lower limit. The executable branch assigns L, so the clause differs even though L conforms to the separately conflicting CL.LNH codelist.

Define-XML ADLBC.ANRIND and workbook Methods!D73 retain the half-upper expression and source spelling LBSTRNHI. Executable _HI_15 uses 1.5*A1HI, with A1HI from LB.LBSTNRHI, which changes both the stated multiplier and source spelling rather than expressing the documented clause.

Define-XML ADLBC.BNRIND and workbook Methods!D76 state comparisons of BASE with the listed limits, albeit with the erroneous ANRIND target and LBSTRNHI source. Executable _BNRIND_RAW propagates baseline ANRIND rather than those comparisons, so the malformed documented computation still has no equivalent executable clause.

The full Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL method and workbook Methods!D70 explicitly require discontinuation before Visit 12 for the early last-assessment case. Neither executable AENTMTFL, _AENT_MAX nor the EOTFB/eot/eot2 paths tests discontinuation status, so the condition is absent from the whole specification.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL and workbook Methods!D70 require the last assessment of the analyte during treatment. _AENT_MAX orders by the largest eligible nominal AVISITN rather than assessment chronology, which does not express that last-assessment condition for out-of-order or unscheduled observations.
